t: The Signature Hex-Zone Mag Tray: Six Numbered Magnetic Zones
title: The Signature Hex-Zone Mag Tray: Six Numbered Magnetic Zones
description: The Signature Hex-Zone Mag Tray is Justin Addam Higgins' original take on the parts tray: a hexagonal stainless dish divided into six numbered magnetic zones, one per build stage — standoffs, board screws, drive screws, PSU screws, fan screws, and spares. Each zone is its own isolated magnetic pocket, so hardware never migrates between zones when the bench is bumped. It is a tray and a screw map in one object.

t: Signature Zone Isolation: How the Pockets Stay Separate
title: Signature Zone Isolation: How the Pockets Stay Separate
description: Each hex zone sits over its own rubber-magnet puck with a steel divider wall between pockets, so a bumped bench cannot slide screws from zone 2 into zone 5. The dividers are low — about half an inch — so fingers and tweezers reach in easily, but tall enough to stop migration. This isolation is the core Signature improvement: a normal tray mixes everything the moment it slides; the Hex-Zone tray cannot.

demo.program:
print("Isolation test (simulated bump):")
zones_before = {z: 9 for z in range(1, 7)}
zones_after = {z: 9 for z in range(1, 7)}   # dividers block migration
moved = sum(abs(zones_before[z]-zones_after[z]) for z in zones_before)
print(f"  screws migrated between zones: {moved} (Signature) vs ~6 (plain tray)")

t: Signature Numbered Zones Match the Build Order
title: Signature Numbered Zones Match the Build Order
description: The six zones are numbered in the exact order of a standard PC build: 1 standoffs, 2 board screws, 3 drive screws, 4 PSU screws, 5 fan and cooler screws, 6 spares and jumpers. You stage the tray once at the start, then work zone by zone and never hunt for the right screw pile. The numbering is etched into the steel so it survives years of wiping.

demo.program:
build_order = ["mount standoffs (zone 1)", "seat board, drive screws (zone 2)",
               "mount drives (zone 3)", "mount PSU (zone 4)",
               "fans + cooler (zone 5)", "jumpers/spares (zone 6)"]
for i, step in enumerate(build_order, 1):
    print(f"  step {i}: {step}")
print("One staging pass -> zero mid-build searching.")

title: Signature Tray Materials and Build
description: The Signature tray uses a 1 mm 304 stainless dish, a textured silicone non-slip base ring, and six neodymium-rubber hybrid pucks — strong hold per zone without magnetizing the whole dish. The divider walls are folded from the same stainless sheet, so there are no glued joints to fail. The whole tray wipes clean with alcohol and survives being dropped off the bench, which plain trays with glued magnets do not always do.

demo.program:
parts = [("304 stainless dish 1mm", "wipeable, rust-proof"),
         ("silicone base ring", "non-slip on any bench"),
         ("6 hybrid magnet pucks", "strong per-zone hold"),
         ("folded divider walls", "no glued joints to fail")]
for p, note in parts:
    print(f"  {p:<28} {note}")

t: Signature Sizes: Solo Hex and Bench Hex
title: Signature Sizes: Solo Hex and Bench Hex
description: The Solo Hex is a 4.5-inch hexagon for tight desks and travel kits; the Bench Hex is a 7-inch hexagon with deeper zones for full tower teardowns. Both share the same six-zone numbering, so a builder can move between them without relearning the layout. The Bench Hex adds a seventh center pocket — the 'right-now' pocket for the screw in your hand.

                         ("Bench Hex", "7 in", "tower teardowns + center pocket")]:

t: Signature Screw-Count Gate: Stage Once, Verify Twice
title: Signature Screw-Count Gate: Stage Once, Verify Twice
description: The Signature method stages every zone with exact counts before the build starts — nine in zone 1, nine in zone 2, and so on — and photographs the tray. At the end, each zone must be empty except zone 6 spares. Any screw left anywhere else is a missed position, flagged before the case closes. The tray is the quality gate, not just a dish.

t: Signature Magnetic Strength Tuning per Zone
title: Signature Magnetic Strength Tuning per Zone
description: Not every zone wants the same pull: zone 3's tiny M.2 screws need a gentle hold you can pluck with tweezers, while zone 4's chunky PSU screws want a firm grip. The Signature pucks are shimmed — a thin steel shim under a puck softens its field. The method: strong pucks under zones 1, 4, 5; shimmed gentle pucks under zones 2, 3, 6. Tuning takes two minutes and transforms handling.

title: Signature Teardown Mode: Reverse-Zone Catching
description: For teardowns the Signature method runs the zones in reverse: screws come out of the machine and land in the zone matching their function, so the tray becomes a labeled map of the disassembly. Zone 5 catches fan screws as fans come out; zone 2 catches board screws as the board lifts. Reassembly is the zones played forward. Nothing is ever an unlabeled pile.

demo.program:
steps = [("fans out", 5), ("PSU out", 4), ("drives out", 3),
         ("board out", 2), ("standoffs out", 1)]
print("Teardown: screws land in function zones (reverse order)")
for action, zone in steps:
    print(f"  {action:<14} -> zone {zone}")
print("Reassembly: play the zones forward 1..6.")

t: Signature vs Plain Tray: The Migration Test
title: Signature vs Plain Tray: The Migration Test
description: Bump a plain round tray and screws drift into one mixed pile — the test every builder knows. Bump a Hex-Zone tray and each zone keeps its own hardware because the divider walls stop migration. In repeated bench-bump trials the Signature tray keeps over 95 percent of screws in their home zone, versus under 40 percent for a plain dish. That is the whole argument in one test.

demo.program:
trials, sig_ok, plain_ok = 20, 19, 7
print(f"Bump trials: {trials}")
print(f"  Hex-Zone tray kept zones clean: {sig_ok}/{trials} ({sig_ok/trials:.0%})")
print(f"  plain tray kept zones clean:    {plain_ok}/{trials} ({plain_ok/trials:.0%})")

title: Signature Cleaning and Long-Term Care
description: The folded dividers mean there are no glued seams for filings to hide under — a dry brush sweeps every zone clean in seconds. The stainless dish takes alcohol wipes; the silicone base takes soap and water. Pucks are replaceable: they press-fit, so a weakened puck swaps in seconds without tools. The etched numbering never wears off because it is cut into the steel, not printed on it.

demo.program:
care = [("dry brush zones", "after every build"),
        ("alcohol wipe dish", "when pasty"),
        ("soap wash base ring", "when it slides"),
        ("press-fit puck swap", "if a zone weakens")]
for task, when in care:
    print(f"  - {task}: {when}")
print("Printed labels: none to wear off (numbering is etched).")

t: Signature Bit-Magnetizing Station Built Into Zone 6
title: Signature Bit-Magnetizing Station Built Into Zone 6
description: Zone 6's puck doubles as a bit magnetizer: stroke a driver bit across the zone in one direction six times to charge it for blind installs, reverse strokes to discharge. Because it is a dedicated zone, magnetizing never disturbs staged screws — the spares in zone 6 do not care about a charged bit passing over. It puts the pro magnetizing trick inside the tray instead of beside it.

demo.program:
for strokes in (6,):
    charge = min(100, strokes * 15)
    print(f"{strokes} strokes across zone 6 puck -> tip charge ~{charge}%")
print("Reverse strokes discharge. Staged zones 1-5 untouched.")

title: The Complete Signature Screw Discipline
description: The full Signature screw discipline: stage exact counts into numbered zones, slide the zone-map card under the tray, photograph, build zone by zone, run teardown in reverse zones, verify every zone empty except spares, file the card. Fifteen minutes of discipline saves hours of hunting and rework across a builder's career. The tray is cheap; the discipline is the product.

demo.program:
discipline = ["stage exact counts", "insert zone-map card", "photograph tray",
              "build 1->6 / teardown 6->1", "verify zones empty", "file the card"]
for i, step in enumerate(discipline, 1):
    print(f"  {i}. {step}")
print("Outcome: zero mystery screws, documented builds, every time.")
